title: Numbers, Time & Dates
subtitle: Count from 0 to 100, tell the time, and say the days and months.
objectives: Count from 0 to 20, then by tens to 100
Name the seven days of the week and twelve months

content.intro: Numbers, time and dates are some of the most useful words you'll ever learn — you'll use them every single day.

rules.heading: Numbers 0–20
rules.body: zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty

rules.heading: Tens, up to 100
rules.body:
twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred

For numbers in between, add the second number: twenty-one, thirty-five, forty-two.

rules.heading: Telling the time
rules.body:
• What time is it? — It's three o'clock. (3:00)
  • It's half past three. (3:30) / It's three thirty.
  • It's a quarter past three. (3:15) / It's a quarter to four. (3:45)

rules.heading: Days and months
rules.body:
Days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday

Months: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December

examples: I have two brothers and one sister.
What time is it? — It's ten o'clock.
The meeting is at half past two.
There are seven days in a week and twelve months in a year.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have twenty and five years.
commonMistakes.why: Ages use "to be," and compound numbers use a hyphen with no "and": twenty-five, not twenty and five.
Days of the week are always capitalized in English.

commonMistakes.right: It's half past three. / It's three thirty.
commonMistakes.why: "Half past" is the standard way to say 30 minutes past the hour.

items.explanation: "A quarter past" means 15 minutes after the hour.

exercises.title: Match the Number to the Word

items.explanation: Practice reading numbers as words — this is essential for telling time, prices and dates.

items.prompt: How many months are there in a year?
items.explanation: There are 12 months in a year.
The order is ...Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday...

summary: Numbers 0–20 have their own words; from 20 on, combine the tens word with the ones word (twenty-five).
What time is it? → It's [hour] o'clock / half past [hour] / a quarter past/to [hour].
Days and months are always capitalized in English.
